summary: The Improving Interagency Coordination for Pipeline Reviews Act changes the federal review process for certain natural gas pipeline projects and liquefied natural gas terminals. It makes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission the sole lead agency for environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act, sets schedules and concurrent reviews for other agencies, removes the requirement for state water quality certifications under Section 401 of the Clean Water Act, and requires agencies to consider remote survey data.

affected_groups.effect: Acts as the sole lead agency for environmental reviews, sets review schedules, consults with the TSA, and tracks progress publicly on its website.
Must navigate a coordinated review process led by FERC, are exempt from obtaining a Section 401 water quality certification, and may submit remote survey data.
affected_groups.group: Natural gas and LNG project applicants

affected_groups.effect: Must participate under FERC-led schedules, defer to FERC's review scope, conduct concurrent reviews, and propose water quality conditions directly to FERC rather than issuing certifications.
Must consult with FERC regarding pipeline infrastructure, cyber, and personnel security measures.

key_provisions: Makes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission the sole lead agency for coordinating environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act for covered natural gas and LNG projects.
Requires other participating agencies to defer to FERC's approved scope for the environmental review to the maximum extent authorized by law.

Removes the requirement for project applicants to obtain a state water quality certification under Section 401 of the Clean Water Act, replacing it with direct state proposal of terms or conditions to FERC.
Prohibits FERC from setting a final authorization deadline more than 90 days after the completion of the environmental review.
Mandates that federal and state agencies carry out their responsibilities concurrently with FERC's environmental review and follow established schedules.
Requires agencies to consider applicant-submitted data gathered by aerial or other remote means.
Requires FERC to consult with the Transportation Security Administration on pipeline security, cybersecurity, and personnel security measures.
missing_information: Specific criteria for how FERC determines project review schedules.
Detailed enforcement mechanisms for agencies that miss statutory deadlines other than notifying Congress and the Commission.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Improving Interagency Coordination for Pipeline Reviews Act changes the federal review process for certain natural gas pipeline projects and liquefied natural gas terminals. It makes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission the sole lead agency for environmental reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act, sets schedules and concurrent reviews for other agencies, removes the requirement for state water quality certifications under Section 401 of the Clean Water Act, and requires agencies to consider remote survey data.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation alters the regulatory framework for natural gas pipelines and LNG terminals by centralizing authority in a single lead agency, establishing strict review timelines, modifying water quality review procedures, and altering how federal and state agencies cooperate during project authorizations.
